title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
authors: Samyam Rajbhandari, Jeff Rasley, Olatunji Ruwase, Yuxiong He
date: October 2019 (arXiv v1); v3 May 2020; published at SC20

code.title: DeepSpeed
code.note: the authors' library, where ZeRO ships (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path)

takeaway: ZeRO shards optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel ranks (16 bytes/param for mixed-precision Adam down to 16 Psi/N_d at stage 3, at most 1.5x DP communication), making memory scale with cluster size and spawning DeepSpeed and FSDP.

headline.d: 2 fp16 weights + 2 fp16 gradients + 12 fp32 optimizer states
for 1.5× the communication of plain data parallelism
15 PFLOPS sustained, up to 10× Megatron's throughput

resources.t: Microsoft Research blog: ZeRO and DeepSpeed
resources.n: the launch post for ZeRO and DeepSpeed, with the stage diagram.
the clearest modern walkthrough of the stage-by-stage memory math and communication schedules, with diagrams.
the practitioner view: config flags for stages 1, 2 and 3, offload, and what each knob costs.

resources.t: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs
resources.n: places ZeRO in the full landscape of data, tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism.
the PyTorch-native descendant of ZeRO-3 (core pages); maps ZeRO stages onto FSDP sharding strategies.

kb.n: 2019: the tensor-parallel baseline ZeRO measures against and composes with; ZeRO-R's P_a partitions Megatron's replicated activations.
2020: the scale regime (175B) this systems line made trainable.
2022: a complementary attack on activation memory, at the kernel level rather than the sharding level.
2021: the mixture-of-experts route to parameter scale, orthogonal to state sharding.
2019: the 11B model, trained with Mesh-TensorFlow model parallelism, that the paper calls the largest in the literature.
2021: the other way to shrink the 12 bytes of optimizer state per parameter, by training far fewer parameters.
2023: adds paged optimizers and 4-bit frozen weights to LoRA, for fine-tuning on one GPU.
2024: trained with ZeRO-1 data parallelism alongside 16-way pipeline and 64-way expert parallelism.
2024: trained with FSDP that shards optimizer states and gradients but keeps parameters gathered between forward and backward.

kb.t: Bounding the memory bottlenecks of large mixture-of-experts training
kb.n: 2026: bounds expert dispatch, vocabulary projection, activation checkpointing and optimiser state inside a fixed memory budget by scheduling when each tensor exists, where ZeRO partitions the same state.

verdict: Believe the memory accounting and the communication argument: they are exact arithmetic that reproduces table for table and became the industry standard. Treat the speed-ups as single, unrepeated runs against a 2019 baseline, and the trillion-parameter claim as analysis: stage 3 was not built in this paper.
